sentences.text: Respondent Nos.2 and 1 were the driver and insurer respectively of Car bearing No.KL-10/AJ-2986; respondent No.3 is owner of KSRTC bus bearing No.KA-07/F-1582.

On 28.05.2013, at 11.00 p.m., when Manjunath was crossing the road near Billakempanahalli Gate on Bengaluru-Mysuru road, the accident took place involving KSRTC bus bearing No.KA- 07/F-1582 and car bearing No.KL-10/AJ-2986.
In the accident, Manjunath got injuries.
He was shifted to Rajarajeshwari Hospital, Bengaluru, where he succumbed to injuries on the same day.
5. On the basis of complaint by one Lokesh, FIR in Crime No.211/2013 in Bidadi Police Station as per Ex.P.1 was registered against the drivers of bus and car.
On investigation, charge sheet as per Ex.P.8 was filed against both of them for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 304(A) of IPC read with 187 of IMV Act.

The wife, children, parents and younger sister of deceased Manjunath filed MVC No.3273/2013 before the MACT, Bengaluru, claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/-
from respondents on the ground that they were all depending on the income of deceased Manjunath and due to his accidental death, they suffered damages.
6. The respondents contested the matter denying rashness and negligence on the part of drivers of car and bus, age, occupation, income of deceased and their liability to pay compensation.
They contended that accident occurred due to negligence of deceased himself as he was trying to cross the road without taking due precaution.
Respondent No.3 contended that the driver of car was rash and negligent, whereas respondent Nos.1 and 2 contended that accident occurred solely due to rash and negligent driving of bus in question.
7. The Tribunal, on hearing parties, by the impugned award held that accident occurred due to contributory negligence of the drivers of bus, car and deceased himself.
The Tribunal apportioned negligence at 60% to bus driver; 30% to car driver and 10% to the deceased.

The Tribunal assessed the income of deceased at Rs.6,000/- per month and added 50% to the same as 'future prospects',
deducted 1/4th from it for his 'personal expenses', considered his age as 30 years, applied 18 multiplier - 10 - and awarded compensation of Rs.18,48,000/- on different heads as per the table below;
1. Loss of dependency Rs.9,72,000/-
(Rs.6,000 x  x 12 x 18)
2. Add 50% Future Prospectus Rs.4,86,000/-
3. Loss of Consortium (P-1) Rs.1,00,000/-
4. Loss of Love and Affection Rs.1,00,000/-
(P-2 and 3)

7 5. Loss of Love and Affection Rs. 50,000/-
(P-4 and 5)
6. Loss of Love and Affection Rs. 10,000/-
(P-6)
7. Loss of Estate (P-1 to 5) Rs.1,00,000/-
8. Loss of Estate (P-6) Rs. 10,000/-
9. Transportation of Dead Body and Rs. 20,000/-
 Funeral Expenses  TOTAL Rs.18,48,0000/-
8.
The claimants challenge the said award on the ground that imputing 10% negligence to deceased is erroneous.
It is also contended that compensation awarded is on the lower side.
Whereas, KSRTC challenges the award on the ground that as per the evidence on record, rashness and negligence was on the part of driver of car and deceased himself and compensation awarded is high.

Similarly,
Insurance Company challenges the award on the ground that imputation of 30%
- 11 - negligence to it is incorrect and compensation awarded is also incorrect.

9. Having regard to rival contentions, questions that arise for consideration are;
"i) Whether the finding of Tribunal with regard to contributory negligence is sustainable in law?
ii) Whether the compensation awarded is just?"
10.

Re. Point No.1:
There is no dispute that in the accident both KSRTC bus and car were involved.

Though PW.2 was cited as eyewitness and examined, his complaint at Ex.P.1 and oral evidence was that when he was proceeding near the scene of incident, he heard loud sound of accident, then he turned and rushed to the accidental spot and on enquiry with people gathered there, he came to know that KSRTC bus came in a high speed and to avoid the deceased who was crossing the road, turned the bus and hit the car,
in turn car hit the deceased.

That is how the Chaitra M vs The Manager on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152279381/
8 - 12 - accident was caused.
He himself has stated in the complaint that driver of bus himself shifted the injured to Hospital and in the complaint, requested to take action against the car driver.
By the aforesaid evidence, it becomes clear that there was no direct witness to the incident.
11. To substantiate it's contention that accident took place due to rash and negligence driving of car bearing No.KL-10/AJ- 2986, respondent No.3 examined the driver of said bus as RW.1.

He deposed that while driving the bus at the scene of incident, he noticed the deceased crossing road and he crossed the deceased, thereafter the car in question came from hind side in high speed in a rash and negligent manner and hit the victim and hit his bus from hind side.
12. Ex.P.3 - sketch of scene of offence shows that deceased had fallen close to the median of road and he was not in the centre of road.
He was crossing the road where opening was left for pedestrians to cross the road.
The bus-stop was near - 13 - the scene of offence.
That probabalises claimants' case that after alighting the bus, he was crossing the road.
Therefore, Tribunal was not justified in imputing 10% negligence to him.
13. Insofar as negligence, manner of occurrence of accident and negligence on the part of driver of bus and car, EX.P.5-IMV report is the material document.

According to respondent Nos.1 and 2,
when the bus was about to hit Manjunath, to avoid him, driver of bus suddenly took that on the right side i.e towards road median and consequently, he hit the car from right hand side which was moving in front of the bus.
If that is the case, there should have been damages on right front side of bus and on left hind side of car.
But, Ex.P.5 shows that the rear side of body of bus was damaged.
Insofar as car, front bumper, left head light indicator, left side front fender etc., were damaged.
If the bus hits from hind side, the possibility of front bumper of car being damaged and rear side of bus being damaged are improbable.
Respondent Nos.1 and 2 did not examine the driver of car to substantiate the said contention.
- 14 - If the car driver was examined, respondent No.3 would have got an opportunity to cross-examine him and demonstrate its case.
For withholding such material witnesses, adverse inference has to be drawn.
14. The main document relied on by the claimants as well as respondent Nos.1 and 2 to impute negligence to bus driver was Ex.P.8-charge sheet.

It is material to note that police filed the charge sheet under Section 187 of IMV Act on the ground that driver of bus after causing accident, without stopping the bus escaped from the scene of incident.
But in the evidence of PW.2 as well as in the complaint, there is clear statement that driver of bus helped in shifting the victim to Hospital.

Under Chaitra M vs The Manager on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152279381/
9 such circumstance, how Section 187 of IMV Act is invoked is the question.

sentences.text: That goes to show that charge sheet was not based on objective material with objective purpose.

Under such circumstance,
charge sheet Ex.P.8 becomes only a guiding document for the Court, but not a binding document of conclusive proof of negligence on the part of bus driver.
In the light of above discussions, Tribunal should have imputed negligence totally to the driver of car instead of imputing to the driver of bus and victim himself.
16. Re. Compensation.

Though the claimants relying on PM Report Ex.P.7 contended that age of deceased was 30 years,
their own document at Ex.P.11-Aadhar card issued on 27.03.2013 shows that Manjunath himself in the said document furnished his year of birth as '1981'.
Therefore, Tribunal should have considered the same rather than PM Report.
Based on that, age of deceased comes to 32 years.
Though it was contended that Manjunath was earning Rs.15,000/- per month by his Masonary work, there is no proof of the same.
However, having regard to his age, nature of his work and wages payable to such skilled labour at that time, Tribunal should have taken his income at Rs.8,000/- per month.

As per the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others - AIR 2017 SC 5157, 40% of the said - 16 - income has to be super added to the same as 'future prospects' which comes to Rs.8,200+Rs.3,000/- = Rs.11,200/- per month.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others - AIR 2017 SC 5157
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since deceased Manjunath had five dependants and as claimant No.6, his younger sister is married, 1/4th had to be deducted from his income for his 'personal expenses.

Therefore, the compensation payable on the head of 'loss of dependency' comes to Rs.11,200x3/4= 8,400x12x16=16,12,800/-.
17.

In view of judgment in Pranay Sethi's case, claimants were entitled to compensation at Rs.44,000/- each on the head of 'loss of consortium' and Rs.33,000/- on conventional heads 'funeral expenses and loss of estate'.

Therefore, the just compensation payable is as follows;
1. Loss of dependency Rs.16,12,800/-
2. Loss of consortium Rs. 2,64,000/-
3. Funeral Expenses and loss of Rs. 33,000/-
 estate  TOTAL Rs.19,09,800/-

10 18.
There is no dispute that at the time of accident, car in question was insured with respondent No.1.

Therefore,
- 17 - respondent No.1 is liable to indemnify the said damages.
For the aforesaid reasons, appeal of Insurer-respondent No.1 is liable to be dismissed, appeal of claimants deserves to be allowed in-part and appeal of KSRTC-respondent No.3 deserves to be allowed.

Hence, the following:
Order i) MFA No.4013/2014 is dismissed.
ii) MFA No.4165/2014 is allowed.
iii) MFA No.5154/2014 is partly allowed.

iv) The impugned order is modified as follows;
a) The claim petition against respondent No.3-  Managing Director of KSRTC is hereby  dismissed.
b) The claimants are entitled to compensation of Rs.19,09,800/- with interest thereon at 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realisation.
- 18 - c) Respondent Nos.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the same.
d) Respondent No.1-Insurer is liable to indemnify the damages.
e) Respondent No.1 shall deposit the award amount before the Tribunal within six weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this award.
f) The amount in deposit in MFA No.4165/2014 shall be refunded to the appellant therein.
g) The amount in deposit in MFA No.4013/2014, if any, shall be transmitted to Trial Court.

5. On the basis of complaint by one Lokesh, FIR in Crime No.211/2013 in Bidadi Police Station as per Ex.P.1 was registered against the drivers of bus and car.
On investigation, charge sheet as per Ex.P.8 was filed against both of them for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 304(A) of IPC read with 187 of IMV Act.
The wife, children, parents and younger sister of deceased Manjunath filed MVC No.3273/2013 before the MACT, Bengaluru, claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/-
from respondents on the ground that they were all depending on the income of deceased Manjunath and due to his accidental death, they suffered damages.
6. The respondents contested the matter denying rashness and negligence on the part of drivers of car and bus, age, occupation, income of deceased and their liability to pay compensation.
They contended that accident occurred due to negligence of deceased himself as he was trying to cross the road without taking due precaution.
Respondent No.3 contended that the driver of car was rash and negligent, whereas respondent Nos.1 and 2 contended that accident occurred solely due to rash and negligent driving of bus in question.
7. The Tribunal, on hearing parties, by the impugned award held that accident occurred due to contributory negligence of the drivers of bus, car and deceased himself.
The Tribunal apportioned negligence at 60% to bus driver; 30% to car driver and 10% to the deceased.

Under such circumstance,
charge sheet Ex.P.8 becomes only a guiding document for the Court, but not a binding document of conclusive proof of negligence on the part of bus driver.
In the light of above discussions, Tribunal should have imputed negligence totally to the driver of car instead of imputing to the driver of bus and victim himself.
However, having regard to his age, nature of his work and wages payable to such skilled labour at that time, Tribunal should have taken his income at Rs.8,000/- per month.
There is no dispute that at the time of accident, car in question was insured with respondent No.1.
